agents.name: Codex

surface_source.quote: I have yet to move my workflow over fully from the CLI tools since I appreciate the flexibility of the terminal.

agents.quote: Opus is where I start, but Codex writes all my code.

history.quote: This is different from what I was doing 6 months ago, where I was mostly using Cursor and the built-in agent or extensions.

agents.name: Claude Code

surface_source.quote: The net result between the two is that I'll start with Claude Code and keep that open as a pane, then flip to Codex when I'm ready to actually start the coding.

agents.quote: Claude Code is my regular driver for planning, orchestrating my terminal, and managing git/github operations.

models.name: Fable 5

history.quote: Opus is where I start, but Codex writes all my code.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.quote: When doing coding work, I almost always reach for the most expensive and capable models (Fable 5, 5.6 Sol).

history.quote: I run on GPT-5.3-Codex-xhigh or high, and the Codex code just straight up has fewer bugs.

review_style.value: Spot-checks the architecture; Cursor Bugbot and Codex review every PR
review_style.quote: I still spot-check the code, and make sure I understand it from an architecture level, but increasingly I am not reading every line of every PR. I rely on agents to spot subtle bugs (they are far better at it than I am).

also.quote: Since then, I've settled mostly on Cursor as the default option since you can tell when it's working, though I find the results of Codex are good too.

harness.value: Ghostty panes, a git worktree per numbered plan, a preview deploy per branch
harness.quote: I have a worktree skill which copies any relevant plans, env vars, and other updates, and starts a new branch.

history.value: Claude and Codex instances in tmux
history.quote: For a little while I was running multiple Claude/Codex instances in tmux, but now I just use multiple panes within the same terminal tab.

parallelism.quote: This is over-hyped on Twitter, but I do really try and kick off 3-4 tasks in Codex before going to bed, so they'll be ready for review in the morning.

rules_files.value: Shared AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md in a private 'claudefiles' repo
rules_files.quote: Today I have a bunch of skills and a shared AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md defined in a repo I call claudefiles.

signature.caption: loops until CI and bots pass
signature.why: Our pick: at the end of /implement-all it pushes, waits for CI, fixes what Bugbot and Codex flag, and goes round again, so review comments get handled without him.
signature.quote: It essentially 1) pushes to the remote 2) waits for all CI to pass 3) runs /address-bugs and then optionally goes to step 1 until it's finished.

archetype.why: He built his own chain of skills, from /commit to /pr-pass, one step at a time, and dropped skills other people wrote.
